title: Import, the State CLI and Logging

header.html: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace; 7b Use the CLI to inspect state; 7c Describe when and how to use verbose logging
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Importing existing infrastructure

Import brings an existing real resource under Terraform's management by adding it to the state. Import does not write the configuration for you by default.

Method How
import block (Terraform 1.5 and later, preferred) Declare to (the resource address) and id (the real object's ID) in configuration
terraform import command (older) terraform import aws_instance.web INSTANCE_ID 
import {
  to = aws_instance.web
  id = "i-0abc1234567890def"
}

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
}
Fact Detail
Two parts The resource block (configuration) and the state entry (import)
Generate configuration terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf can write the resource block for import blocks
With import blocks Reviewed in plan and applied with apply like any change
With the command The state changes immediately; you must write the matching resource block yourself
The id Depends on the resource type (see the provider documentation)
Exam tip

. Import fills the state, not the configuration (unless you generate it). After an import, plan should show no changes if your configuration matches.

2Inspecting state with the CLI

The terraform state command reads and changes state safely. Never edit the state file by hand.

Command What it does
terraform state list Lists resource addresses in the state
terraform state show ADDRESS Shows the attributes of one resource
terraform state mv SOURCE DEST Moves an item to a new address
terraform state rm ADDRESS Removes an item from state without destroying the real object
terraform state pull Prints the raw state (JSON)
terraform state push Uploads a state file (rare and risky)
terraform show Human-readable view of the whole state or a saved plan
terraform output Shows output values
Exam tip

. state list shows what exists, state show shows one resource, state rm forgets without destroying.

3Verbose logging

Terraform writes detailed logs when you set environment variables.

Variable Meaning
TF_LOG Sets the level: TRACE (most detail), DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
TF_LOG_PATH Writes the log to a file instead of the screen
TF_LOG_CORE, TF_LOG_PROVIDER Separate levels for Terraform core and for providers 
export TF_LOG=DEBUG
export TF_LOG_PATH=terraform-debug.log
terraform plan
When to use Reason
A provider error is unclear See the API calls
Terraform seems to hang See where it waits
Reporting a bug Attach the log (after removing secrets)

Logs can contain sensitive data, so treat them like secrets. Unset TF_LOG when finished.

Exam tip

. TF_LOG=TRACE is the most verbose. Use TF_LOG_PATH to save the log to a file.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team has a manually created instance and wants Terraform to manage it from now on. What does import do?

  • ACreates a second copy of the instance
  • BAdds the existing object to the state
  • CDeletes the instance and recreates it
  • DGenerates a new state backend
Show the answer

Answer: B. Import adds the existing real object to the state so Terraform can manage it.

S2With the older terraform import command, what must the user also provide?

  • AA matching resource block in the configuration
  • BA new provider alias
  • CA new backend block
  • DA lock file for the object
Show the answer

Answer: A. The command only changes the state; the matching resource block must be written by the user.

S3Which feature can write a resource block for an import block automatically?

  • Aterraform fmt -generate
  • Bterraform validate -generate
  • Cterraform plan -generate-config-out
  • Dterraform output -generate
Show the answer

Answer: C. The -generate-config-out option can generate configuration for import blocks.

S4Which command lists every resource address in the state?

  • Aterraform state show
  • Bterraform output
  • Cterraform providers
  • Dterraform state list
Show the answer

Answer: D. terraform state list prints the addresses of the resources in the state.

S5Which command removes a resource from state without destroying the real object?

  • Aterraform destroy -target
  • Bterraform fmt -remove
  • Cterraform apply -replace
  • Dterraform state rm
Show the answer

Answer: D. terraform state rm removes the item from state and leaves the real resource running.

S6Which setting writes detailed debug information to a file?

  • ATF_VAR_log set to true
  • BTF_LOG_PATH with a file name, with TF_LOG set to a level
  • CA logging block in the provider
  • DThe -verbose flag of terraform fmt
Show the answer

Answer: B. TF_LOG sets the level and TF_LOG_PATH sends the log to a file.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does import add?

Show the answer

An existing real object to the state.

R2What are the two arguments of an import block?

Show the answer

to and id.

R3Which command shows one resource's attributes?

Show the answer

terraform state show.

R4Which log level is the most detailed?

Show the answer

TRACE.

R5Which variable saves the log to a file?

Show the answer

TF_LOG_PATH.

R6Can logs contain secrets?

Show the answer

Yes, so treat them as sensitive.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Import adds the object to state; import block (to, id) or terraform import; -generate-config-out
State CLI list, show, mv, rm, pull; terraform show; never edit by hand
Logging TF_LOG (TRACE to ERROR), TF_LOG_PATH, TF_LOG_CORE, TF_LOG_PROVIDER; logs may hold secrets
